Slopes of a Covariate by Group

Source: R/pm_slopes.R
pm_slopes.Rd

The slope (rate of change) of the fitted response in a numeric covariate within each level of a model term, with standard errors, degrees of freedom, confidence limits and tests, and pairwise comparisons of the slopes, as emmeans::emtrends() and SAS ESTIMATE statements on slope terms.

Usage

pm_slopes(model, covariate, modelterm, at = NULL, conf_level = 0.95, adj = "none",
          df_method = c("auto", "Kenward-Roger", "Satterthwaite", "containment",
            "between-within", "KR-expected", "KR-average", "inner-outer", "residual"),
          vcov_adjust = TRUE,
          weights = c("equal", "proportional", "outer", "cells", "flat"),
          vcov = NULL, ...)

Arguments

model

A fitted model, as for predictmeans.

covariate

Name (in "quotes") of the numeric covariate.

modelterm

Name (in "quotes") of the factor term whose levels get a slope each, e.g. "Variety".

at

The value of the covariate where the slopes are taken (matters only when the covariate enters the model non-linearly); the default is its mean.

conf_level

Confidence level of the limits, the default is 0.95 (level = 0.05 before 2.0).

adj

Adjustment of the p-values of the pairwise comparisons of slopes, as in predictmeans.

df_method, vcov_adjust, weights, vcov

As in predictmeans.

...

Not used: level (before 2.0) stops with its 2.0 spelling.

Value

An object of class "pm_slopes", a list in the layout of predictmeans (tidy() and as.data.frame() return its tables, what = "slopes" or "pairs"):

slopes

one row per level of modelterm: the factor columns, estimate (the slope), std.error, df, statistic (t), p.value (of slope = 0), conf.low and conf.high.

pairs

one row per pair of levels: level1, level2, estimate (slope of level1 minus slope of level2), std.error, df, statistic, p.value, p.adj, conf.low, conf.high and, with the adjustments that have them (tukey, bonferroni, sidak, scheffe, mvt), adj.conf.low, adj.conf.high: simultaneous limits that leave out 0 exactly when p.adj is below 1 - conf_level.

settings

modelterm, covariate, at, level, adjust, df_method, vcov_adjust, vcov, model_class, version.

Details

The slopes are on the scale of the linear predictor. They come from the reference grid of Kmatrix: the change in the K matrix between at - h and at + h, divided by 2h with h = 0.0001 times the standard deviation of the covariate. This is exact when the covariate enters the model linearly (also through interactions) and a central difference for poly(), splines and smooths, whose slope depends on at. Standard errors and degrees of freedom follow predictmeans: for models fitted by REML (lmer, lme, gls) Kenward-Roger (with the adjusted covariance when vcov_adjust = TRUE); with one df per term (containment, between-within, nlme's df) the smallest df of the terms with the covariate; otherwise the residual df.

See also

covariatemeans, predictmeans, advice

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

  library(predictmeans)
  Oats <- as.data.frame(nlme::Oats)
  fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety + (1|Block/Variety), data = Oats)
  sl <- pm_slopes(fm, "nitro", "Variety", adj = "tukey")
  sl
#> Slopes of ‘nitro’ at 0.3 (95% limits; Kenward-Roger df) 
#> 
#>      Variety estimate std.error df statistic   p.value conf.low conf.high
#>  Golden Rain    75.33     11.86 51     6.353 5.726e-08    51.53     99.14
#>   Marvellous    64.58     11.86 51     5.446 1.490e-06    40.78     88.39
#>      Victory    81.08     11.86 51     6.838 9.828e-09    57.28    104.89
#>  estimable
#>       TRUE
#>       TRUE
#>       TRUE
#> 
#> Pairwise differences of slopes (p.adj: tukey)
#> 
#>       level1     level2 estimate std.error df statistic p.value  p.adj conf.low
#>  Golden Rain Marvellous    10.75     16.77 51    0.6410  0.5244 0.7982   -22.92
#>  Golden Rain    Victory    -5.75     16.77 51   -0.3429  0.7331 0.9373   -39.42
#>   Marvellous    Victory   -16.50     16.77 51   -0.9839  0.3298 0.5903   -50.17
#>  conf.high adj.conf.low adj.conf.high
#>      44.42       -29.73         51.23
#>      27.92       -46.23         34.73
#>      17.17       -56.98         23.98
  as.data.frame(sl, what = "pairs")
#>        level1     level2 estimate std.error       df  statistic   p.value
#> 1 Golden Rain Marvellous    10.75  16.77051 50.99999  0.6410061 0.5243889
#> 2 Golden Rain    Victory    -5.75  16.77051 50.99999 -0.3428637 0.7331102
#> 3  Marvellous    Victory   -16.50  16.77051 50.99999 -0.9838699 0.3298242
#>       p.adj conf.low conf.high adj.conf.low adj.conf.high
#> 1 0.7982489 -22.9182   44.4182    -29.73367      51.23367
#> 2 0.9373365 -39.4182   27.9182    -46.23367      34.73367
#> 3 0.5903123 -50.1682   17.1682    -56.98367      23.98367
